pros.claim: A complete record set is what converts a list of customers into a transferable asset and a defensible position in a dispute
pros.example: a chargeback answered with the dated disclosure record, the signed agreement version and the service history for the period in question

cons.claim: Contemporaneous record-keeping is a real time cost on people who are already running a full route, and it degrades first under pressure
cons.example: a peak-season week where visit notes are written from memory that evening and lose the detail that would have qualified an add-on

failure_modes: keeping records in a partner operator's system with no retained copy
reconstructing service notes after the fact
leaving side promises out of the record until a customer produces them in a dispute
acceptance_tests: a sample of accounts drawn at random each carries the full minimum record set with dated entries
the system of record is named in writing with the partner operator, along with what the seller retains and how
revisit_triggers: a dispute or chargeback cannot be answered from the record
the partner operator changes systems or access rights
record completeness falls in a peak season sample

base.update_signal: a record-completeness sample, a dispute the record could not answer, or a change in the partner operator's systems

nodes.definition: Value the book the way a buyer or a partner operator does: as a stream of expected future visits weighted by how cheaply they can be served and how likely they are to persist. The drivers are few and none of them is the headline account count. Density comes first, because the buyer inherits the drive time along with the revenue: accounts packed into two contiguous route days are worth considerably more than the same number scattered across a county, and a book's map tells more of the story than its list. Then tenure and cohort survival, since an aged book with a stable survival curve is a forecast while a book of first-year accounts is a hope. Then agreement quality and transferability - whether agreements are assignable, whether renewal and payment consents survive a transfer, and whether the record set exists at all to be transferred. Then payment quality, add-on penetration, and callback load, which is the best available proxy for how much unpaid work the book carries with it. Multiples do circulate in this market, but they are outputs of these drivers and of a negotiation between two specific parties, so the honest practice is to model the drivers, get the multiple from the actual counterparty in the actual deal, and never repeat one as though it were a fact about the industry.

included: the value drivers and their ordering
density and callback load as value adjustments
transferability of agreements, consents and records
treating any multiple as an output of drivers and negotiation
excluded: quoting or endorsing any account multiple or valuation figure
deal structuring, tax and legal advice on a sale
the partnering terms that decide who owns the accounts

pros.claim: Modeling the drivers lets a seller improve what the book is worth deliberately rather than hoping a multiple applies to them
pros.example: a season spent tightening one zone and closing record gaps, so the book presents as two dense route days with complete files

cons.claim: The drivers are only partly under the seller's control and a counterparty may weight them differently or not at all
cons.example: a buyer who values only the accounts inside their existing territory and prices the rest as though they were leads

failure_modes: presenting a book by account count with no density or survival view
repeating a market multiple as though it were a fact
ignoring callback load and unresolved structural properties when describing quality
acceptance_tests: the book presentation shows density, cohort survival, transferability, payment quality and callback load, with every figure traceable to the records and no multiple asserted as market fact
revisit_triggers: a zone's density changes materially through growth, pauses or releases
cohort survival shifts
the partnering terms governing assignability or ownership change

base.update_signal: a change in zone density, cohort survival or the assignability terms behind the accounts

nodes.definition: Run a periodic review of the whole book that ends in an explicit decision for every account: keep as is, move to a better route day, reprice at renewal, step the frequency down, or release. The inputs are the products of everything upstream - the account's position and travel on its route, tenure and cohort survival, callback load, payment history, access difficulty, add-on penetration, and the stated reasons of accounts already lost around it. The output is a decision list with a sequence, an owner and a date, not a general intention to tidy up. Release is the uncomfortable decision and it needs written rules: an account that reliably costs a dedicated trip, one that generates repeated unpaid re-services from a structural condition the customer will not address, and one sitting alone in a zone the route has abandoned are all candidates, and keeping them out of sentiment is a decision to subsidize them from the rest of the book. Releasing is done in good order - the term honored or ended exactly as the agreement provides, notice given in good time, a referral offered to an operator who does cover the area, records closed out and the reason recorded - because the released customer keeps talking to neighbors who are still on the book. Triage is not an annual clean-up; it is the mechanism by which a book stays dense while it grows.

included: the periodic review inputs and the five possible decisions
written release criteria
the good-order release procedure including notice and a referral
sequencing and ownership of the decision list
excluded: route sequencing and dispatch changes themselves
terminating a partnering relationship, which the partnering knowledge base handles
any decision that would leave a customer without service in breach of the agreement

pros.claim: An explicit decision for every account stops a book drifting into a scattered collection of accounts nobody chose to keep
pros.example: a quarterly review that moves eleven accounts to a better day, releases three isolated ones and leaves the two dense zones untouched

cons.claim: Release removes revenue immediately and its density benefit arrives slowly, so the decision always looks wrong in the month it is made
cons.example: dropping the outlying accounts of a thin zone and watching the monthly total fall a season before the tightened route pays it back

failure_modes: reviewing the book and producing no decisions
releasing accounts without notice, a referral or a proper closing of the record
keeping every account out of sentiment while the route dilutes around them
acceptance_tests: every account carries a dated decision from the last review with an owner
each release shows the criterion met, the notice given, the referral offered and the record closed with a reason
revisit_triggers: a zone's density falls below what its route day needs
callback load or access difficulty concentrates in a set of accounts
a partner operator changes the territory it will service

base.update_signal: a review cycle's measured density, callback load and survival change which accounts meet the release criteria

edges.why_related: the interval is one of the promises the agreement fixes, so the promise inventory has to exist before a frequency class can be chosen and described
the disclosure set is assembled from the promises and exclusions the agreement actually contains
renewal behavior has to be disclosed at the sale before the renewal event can be designed as a notified checkpoint
how and when money will be taken is part of the pre-signature disclosure, so the billing method must be settled and stated before it is used
the number of recurring visits per year set by the frequency class is the stream side of the payback model
the payback point is what makes the first visits a distinct risk phase rather than an ordinary stretch of the term
the evidence loop is what shows a customer that the covered work is being done, which is what makes the entitlement credible rather than theoretical
the per-visit record is the payload the cadence delivers, so there is nothing to send on a rhythm until the loop produces it
the payback structure decides which survival points are worth measuring, which is why cohorts are tracked by visit number rather than by calendar year
the reason taxonomy explains the movements the survival board detects and shares its account-level source data
the save conversation both captures the reason and is designed around the reasons the taxonomy has already surfaced
the ladder is only reached after the honor-the-request rule and the diagnosis that the conversation performs
the renewal and stored-authorization mechanics are exactly the points where heightened care has to attach
the dated findings that qualify an add-on are produced by the evidence loop at the time of the visit, so there is nothing to qualify an offer without it
the class calendar is only usable once the need test decides which properties may be offered anything at all
the ride-along test is applied class by class, since it is the class that determines whether the work fits inside an existing visit
the notices the cadence sends are part of the record set an account must carry, so the rhythm has to exist before the log can be complete
transferability and every value driver are claims about the record set, so a book cannot be valued honestly before its records exist
triage decisions are made against the value drivers, so the valuation view has to exist before any account is kept, repriced or released
a price may only move in the way that was disclosed at the sale and that the agreement permits, which bounds when and how a wave can be run
work already owed under the between-visit entitlement must never be repackaged as a chargeable add-on, which removes a whole class of tempting offers
only remedies the agreement allows and the servicing operator can actually deliver may be offered on any rung
where care duties apply the ladder is not climbed at all and the cancellation is processed as asked
no account may be repriced, stepped down or released on a judgement the record cannot support, and a release must close the record properly
a stored payment authorization may not outlive the consent the renewal notice established, so the billing routine is bounded by the renewal design
reschedule accommodations and add-on cycles compete for the same route day, so what has already been promised on access limits what can be sold as a ride-along
an account cancelling before payback, especially inside a commission clawback window, creates enormous pressure to slow the exit down
edges.resolution_rule: the honor-the-request rule wins without exception; the economics may justify spending on a genuine remedy or a faster response, never on an obstacle, a delay or a fear argument

edges.why_related: a ride-along add-on is so cheap to deliver that the route tempts a blanket offer to every property on the day regardless of what the record shows
edges.resolution_rule: documented need gates every offer; route fit only decides the order and clustering of offers that have already qualified, and never manufactures one

edges.why_related: discretionary concessions handed out during a price wave quietly undo the wave and, on a dense street, become the price everyone expects
edges.resolution_rule: accounts inside an active wave get defect remedies rather than concessions until the wave's churn response has been measured; any concession granted is recorded against the wave and reviewed before the next segment is released

edges.why_related: free re-services consume the visit capacity the recurring price was meant to cover, so the entitlement and the contribution model pull against each other in a heavy season
edges.resolution_rule: the entitlement is honored exactly as written and is never rationed by friction; a premise generating repeated re-services is escalated to the licensed operator for a structural inspection and, failing resolution, enters book triage

edges.why_related: pausing preserves a relationship the retention count likes while thinning the route density the book's value depends on
edges.resolution_rule: pause only where the need is genuinely seasonal and the reactivation is dated and owned; paused accounts are counted separately from active ones in every retention, density and valuation view

edges.why_related: the unwarned post-treatment activity surge produces a distinctive cluster of it-did-not-work departures in the first weeks that the taxonomy can only see if it is separated from ordinary dissatisfaction
missed and partial visits caused by access failures surface as price cancellations, which is why the taxonomy reconciles stated reasons against the visit record
payment failures retire accounts that never chose to leave and distort the churn picture unless the measurement counts them as their own category
an account is worked in a fixed order across its term, from the early-visit window through the steady middle to the renewal checkpoint, and each stage hands the next a different customer
enrollment ahead of the pressure wave and the designed off-season pause are the two ends of one annual cycle for the same seasonal account
what departing customers say they never saw is the best available specification for what the per-visit record should contain next season
triage results show which frequency classes survive and pay in which zones, which changes what is offered to the next customer on that street
both are contemporaneous-record disciplines: written at the time by the person who saw the thing, in the customer's own words where possible, and close to worthless when reconstructed afterward

conflict_axes.name: payback_pressure_versus_an_easy_exit
conflict_axes.description: An account that leaves before it has repaid its initial service and commission is the most expensive event in the model, which creates constant pressure to make leaving slower and harder; the ethics of the business, and the referral chain in a dense neighborhood, require the exit to be as easy as the entry.
poles: protect the payback by slowing the exit
honor the request immediately and cleanly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend the economics on speed of remedy and quality of diagnosis before the customer decides, never on friction after they have decided; a clear request is always processed

conflict_axes.name: route_efficiency_versus_customer_preferred_timing
conflict_axes.description: The route is efficient because neighboring properties are served on the same pass, while customers want windows that suit their gates, pets, work and tenants; every accommodation granted outside the day chips at the density that pays for the visit.
poles: hold the route day
accommodate the customer's timing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accommodate inside the existing day for the area wherever possible, record access facts so fewer accommodations are needed at all, and treat a standing off-day requirement as a triage input rather than a permanent quiet cost

conflict_axes.name: evidence_gated_upsell_versus_seasonal_revenue_push
conflict_axes.description: Seasonal add-ons carry the best margin in the book and their windows are short, which pushes toward blanket offers; the qualification rule allows an offer only where a dated finding or a genuine property condition exists.
poles: work the season hard across the whole book
offer only where the record qualifies it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pre-load the season by making sure findings are being recorded properly in the visits beforehand, then offer only qualified properties; an unqualified property gets an inspection, not an offer

conflict_axes.name: guarantee_generosity_versus_visit_capacity
conflict_axes.description: The between-visit entitlement is the reason customers accept a recurring agreement, and it is also unpriced capacity that a bad season or a structurally infested premise can consume without limit.
poles: honor every request immediately
protect the route's capacity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honor the entitlement as written and never ration it by friction; solve the capacity problem at its source by escalating repeat-callback premises to the operator for structural inspection and, if unresolved, into triage

conflict_axes.name: price_integrity_versus_save_concessions
conflict_axes.description: Concessions save individual accounts today while permanently lowering their value and, on a street where neighbors compare invoices, resetting what everyone expects to pay.
poles: hold the price and fix the defect
concede to keep the account
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb the remedy ladder in order and treat price as the last rung; record every concession against the account and the price wave so its true cost is visible at the next review

conflict_axes.name: interval_that_controls_versus_interval_that_sells
conflict_axes.description: A shorter interval controls pressure better and raises annual value but is harder to sell and heavier on route capacity, while a longer interval closes easily and then underperforms on a premise that needed more.
poles: sell the interval the pressure requires
sell the interval the customer will buy
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the operator's documented pressure set the floor, describe a longer interval honestly as a lower level of control rather than a discount, and let the survival curves by frequency class settle the argument over time

conflict_axes.name: silent_renewal_convenience_versus_informed_consent
conflict_axes.description: Automatic renewal on a stored payment method is frictionless and retains accounts that would otherwise lapse through inattention, and it is precisely the mechanism that generates chargebacks, complaints and consent harm when the customer did not understand it.
poles: let the agreement continue quietly
make every continuation a noticed, consented event
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: design to the stricter of the verified obligation class and the operator's policy, notify with evidence of value attached, and use nominated third-party contacts where care duties apply

conflict_axes.name: keeping_every_account_versus_keeping_the_book_dense
conflict_axes.description: Every account is revenue and nobody enjoys releasing a paying customer, yet isolated accounts consume route capacity that the dense part of the book is subsidizing.
poles: keep every paying account
keep only what the route can serve well
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make release a written-criteria decision at a periodic review rather than a mood, and release in good order with notice and a referral so the neighbors who stay hear a fair story

conflict_axes.name: flattering_numbers_versus_measured_truth
conflict_axes.description: A blended retention percentage and a headcount of accounts always look better than cohort survival with separated loss types and a density map, and the flattering view is the one that gets quoted to partners and buyers.
poles: report the simple headline
report cohorts, counts and loss mix
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: publish counts and cohort sizes beside every rate, keep paused and payment-failed accounts in their own categories, and refuse to present any figure that cannot be traced to the account records

conflict_axes.name: full_disclosure_versus_close_rate
conflict_axes.description: Stating the initial charge, the term commitment, the renewal behavior and the cancellation route before signature costs sales that a vaguer close would take, and every one of those omissions returns later as a dispute, a chargeback or a review.
poles: disclose everything before signature
close first and explain in the paperwork
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the spoken disclosure set as a floor that is never traded for a close, and measure its cost against first-invoice disputes and early cancellations rather than against the count of doors closed

edge_cases.description: A customer sees more insects in the days after the initial service and calls it proof the treatment failed or made things worse
edge_cases.trigger: the post-treatment activity surge lands on a household that was never warned it happens
edge_cases.mitigation: deliver the surge warning before the initial service and record that it was given, treat the call as a priority re-service request rather than an objection, and have the technician's visit record show what was found on the return

edge_cases.description: An exterior-only visit is performed while nobody is home and the customer believes nobody came
edge_cases.trigger: a routine visit at an unoccupied property with no evidence delivered to the customer
edge_cases.mitigation: require a same-day service record naming what was inspected, treated and removed at that specific property, sent on the channel the customer uses, with the pre-visit notice sent beforehand

edge_cases.description: A long-tenured account lapses because a card expired and nobody noticed until service stopped
edge_cases.trigger: a payment failure that ages without a contact attempt
edge_cases.mitigation: detect failures on a fixed cadence, contact on a channel the customer answers inside a stated grace window, keep service running while it is fixed, and count the loss as involuntary rather than as a cancellation

edge_cases.description: A tenant signed the agreement, then moves out mid-term while the landlord who owns the property never agreed to anything
edge_cases.trigger: occupancy changes at a property whose agreement was signed by someone who does not own it
edge_cases.mitigation: record at signing who is contracting, who pays and who controls access; on a move, close the agreement per its terms with the signer and treat the property as a fresh, fully disclosed sale to the owner or the new occupant rather than as an inherited account

edge_cases.description: A property is sold mid-term and the new owner discovers a recurring service they never agreed to
edge_cases.trigger: a change of ownership at a serviced address
edge_cases.mitigation: close the account against the departing owner per the agreement, record the loss as a move rather than a cancellation, and approach the new occupant as a new sale with full disclosure while noting the route value of an address already known to the technician

edge_cases.description: One premise generates repeated re-service requests every few weeks that the recurring fee never covers
edge_cases.trigger: a structural or neighboring condition, such as an unsealed crawl space or an adjacent neglected property, keeps regenerating pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: honor the entitlement while escalating to the licensed operator for a structural inspection, offer the qualifying exclusion or add-on work from that documented finding, and if the condition remains unaddressed take the account into triage rather than rationing the service quietly

edge_cases.description: A customer states clearly that they want to cancel and the conversation continues with further offers
edge_cases.trigger: a save script that treats a clear request as an objection to be handled
edge_cases.mitigation: stop at the request, process the cancellation, confirm it in writing with its effective date and any remaining obligation, and review the script and the call notes that allowed the drift

edge_cases.description: An adult child calls to say an elderly parent did not understand the agreement that has been renewing automatically
edge_cases.trigger: a third party raises a comprehension or consent concern about a recurring account
edge_cases.mitigation: stop billing activity on the account, escalate to the operator, produce the disclosure and consent record, process a cancellation without any save attempt if that is what is asked, and add a nominated-contact route for any account that continues

edge_cases.description: A technician notices a mud tube or damaged timber during a routine visit at a customer already asking about a swarm they saw
edge_cases.trigger: a suspected wood-destroying-organism condition surfaces inside a general pest account
edge_cases.mitigation: record the observation factually without naming a diagnosis, refer it to the licensed operator for the regulated inspection class, and make no claim, quote or add-on offer that depends on a finding the seller is not licensed to make

edge_cases.description: A mosquito customer paused in autumn is never contacted again and is discovered the following summer as a lost account
edge_cases.trigger: a suspension recorded with no reactivation date or owner
edge_cases.mitigation: set the reactivation date, owner and contact channel at the moment of pausing, re-confirm consent and payment status on return, and count paused accounts in their own category so they cannot hide inside the active book

edge_cases.description: The partner operator loses capacity or withdraws from part of the territory mid-season while agreements are live
edge_cases.trigger: a servicing partner's staffing, licensing or territory changes while accounts are under contract
edge_cases.mitigation: identify which live agreements and re-service entitlements are affected, tell those customers before they discover it through a missed visit, arrange servicing or an orderly release with a referral, and treat the retained record set as the thing that makes any transfer possible

edge_cases.description: A price increase notice lands in the same week a customer's visit was missed or performed only partially
edge_cases.trigger: a price wave released without holding out accounts with open service problems
edge_cases.mitigation: exclude accounts with an open complaint, an unresolved callback or a partial visit from the wave, resolve the service issue first, and re-time the notice for those accounts to a later renewal

workflow.action: Take the agreement apart into a promise inventory
workflow.description: List every promise the current agreement version makes - covered premise and pests, exclusions, initial service, frequency, between-visit entitlement, price basis, term, renewal and cancellation route, access duties - and check it against what the sales conversation implies
workflow.artifact: promise-and-exclusion inventory keyed to the agreement version
workflow.gate: every sales claim maps to a clause and every material exclusion appears on the one-page seller version

workflow.action: Set the frequency-class rule and its route calendar
workflow.description: Define which documented pressure and premise conditions justify each interval, and align each class calendar with the route day that serves the area
workflow.artifact: frequency selection rule with the route day each class lands on
workflow.gate: each class cites its pressure evidence requirement and a servable route day, and none is priced as a discounted version of another

workflow.action: Write and rehearse the pre-signature disclosure set
workflow.description: Fix the words said out loud before any signature or card capture, covering the initial charge, recurring charge, term, renewal behavior, cancellation route, early-termination consequence and exclusions, plus the field that records delivery
workflow.artifact: spoken disclosure script with a dated delivery record field
workflow.gate: the script covers every item, the record field exists on the account, and a sample customer can restate term, renewal and cancellation route at follow-up

workflow.action: Design the renewal event and list the obligation classes to verify
workflow.description: Set the renewal date, the notice route and the value summary that travels with it, and list the automatic-renewal, notice and stored-authorization obligation classes with a named owner for verifying their current content
workflow.artifact: renewal calendar with notice route and a dated obligation-verification list
workflow.gate: every account has a renewal date and notice route, the stated cancellation route works when used, and each obligation class shows an owner and a verification date

workflow.action: Choose the billing method and stand up the payment-failure routine
workflow.description: Decide per-visit, installment or prepaid billing and explain it in the disclosure, then build detection, contact and grace-window handling for failed payments with re-confirmation when amount or term changes
workflow.artifact: billing method statement and payment-failure recovery routine
workflow.gate: every payment failure shows a dated contact attempt inside the stated window before any service interruption

workflow.action: Build the payback model from operator-supplied inputs
workflow.description: Assemble the front-loaded initial cost, commission and clawback exposure, and the recurring contribution into a payback view whose every input names its source
workflow.artifact: per-account payback model with a source note against each input
workflow.gate: no input is an assumed industry figure and the payback point moves visibly when each lever is changed

workflow.action: Specify the per-visit evidence record and the contact rhythm
workflow.description: Define what each visit must report to the customer, with special handling for exterior-only visits at empty properties, and fix the contact beats around it including the pre-visit notice, early-window check-in, seasonal note and renewal notice
workflow.artifact: visit evidence specification and the term contact calendar
workflow.gate: a sampled week of visits each produced a property-specific customer-delivered record, and the beats were sent to the right person on the right channel

workflow.action: Capture access facts and open a one-touch reschedule route
workflow.description: Record gates, dogs, pet-safety instructions, interior-access need, preferred windows and who must be notified at the point of sale, and offer a reschedule path that resolves in one contact inside the existing route day
workflow.artifact: per-account access register and reschedule procedure
workflow.gate: every account has access facts before its first visit and every partial visit names the access constraint that caused it

workflow.action: Instrument cohort survival and the cancellation-reason taxonomy
workflow.description: Stand up survival by start-month cohort and visit number, separate voluntary, involuntary and moved-away losses, segment by zone, channel and frequency class, and capture a category plus the customer's own words at every departure
workflow.artifact: cohort survival board with the loss-mix and reason view
workflow.gate: every figure traces to account records, cohort sizes are shown beside rates, and every closed account carries a reason plus the record reconciliation

workflow.action: Write the save practice: honor the request, then climb the ladder
workflow.description: Document the honor-the-request rule, the equal-ease exit, the diagnosis step, the ordered remedy ladder with price last, and the heightened-care rules that suspend saving altogether where consent or comprehension is doubtful
workflow.artifact: save practice document with the remedy ladder and care rules
workflow.gate: no script contains a consequence-of-stopping claim, every cancellation is confirmed in writing, and each save records the diagnosed reason and the rung used

workflow.action: Gate add-on offers behind documented need and lay out the class calendar
workflow.description: Require a dated record entry, a property or seasonal condition, or a customer report before any offer, then map each add-on class to its pressure window, its referral point for regulated inspection classes, and its ride-along or separate-trip label
workflow.artifact: add-on qualification rule with the class calendar and route labels
workflow.gate: every sold add-on cites its qualifying entry, regulated classes appear as referrals, and separate-trip work records the cluster it belongs to

workflow.action: Close the records, value the book on its drivers, and run the triage review
workflow.description: Complete the per-account record set and the system-of-record agreement with the partner operator, present the book by density, survival, transferability, payment quality, add-on penetration and callback load, then decide keep, reschedule, reprice, step down or release for every account
workflow.artifact: book review pack and a dated decision list with owners
workflow.gate: a random account sample carries the full record set, no multiple is asserted as market fact, and every account has a dated decision with each release showing criterion, notice, referral and closed record

dominance_rules.rule: The licensed-application boundary dominates every retention, save and upsell move
dominance_rules.rationale: pesticide application requires operator and applicator licensing that is jurisdiction-specific and non-negotiable, and no revenue justifies stepping over it
dominance_rules.trigger: a retention, remedy or add-on idea would involve applying, directing or specifying treatment, or would sell work the servicing operator is not licensed and staffed to deliver
dominance_rules.action: drop the idea and route the need to the licensed operator, recording the referral on the account

dominance_rules.rule: A clear cancellation request dominates every retention target, payback horizon and commission clawback exposure
dominance_rules.rationale: obstruction at the exit is the same coercion as pressure at the door and it destroys the referral chain the dense book depends on
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer states clearly that they want to cancel
dominance_rules.action: process the cancellation promptly by a route no harder than sign-up, confirm it in writing, and capture the reason without further offers

dominance_rules.rule: A documented finding dominates any seasonal revenue target
dominance_rules.rationale: findings are shown, never invented, and a business that manufactures infestations has nothing left to sell honestly
dominance_rules.trigger: an add-on offer is contemplated for a property with no qualifying entry in its own record
dominance_rules.action: make no offer; schedule or request an inspection by the licensed operator instead and let its recorded findings decide

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure before signature dominates close rate
dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed initial charge, term or renewal produces the dispute, chargeback and review that cost more than the account earns
dominance_rules.trigger: a close could be completed faster by leaving a charge, the term, the renewal behavior or the cancellation route unsaid
dominance_rules.action: say all of it before the signature or the payment authorization, and record that it was said

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-customer care dominates any save, renewal or add-on opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: the recurring model concentrates consent risk at authorization, silent renewal and the save call, where the harm is largest and least visible
dominance_rules.trigger: comprehension or consent looks doubtful, or a third party raises a concern about an account
dominance_rules.action: stop, escalate to the operator, use the nominated contact route, and process any cancellation with no save attempt

dominance_rules.rule: An owed re-service dominates discretionary and revenue-generating work
dominance_rules.rationale: the between-visit entitlement is the promise the recurring agreement was bought for, and slow-walking it converts the customer's moment of doubt into a departure and a story
dominance_rules.trigger: route capacity must be shared between an owed re-service and a chargeable add-on or a discretionary visit
dominance_rules.action: serve the entitlement first within the committed response window and reschedule the chargeable work

dominance_rules.rule: The verified obligation class dominates operator custom and industry habit
dominance_rules.rationale: renewal, notice, cancellation-route and stored-authorization duties differ by jurisdiction and change, and what an operator has always done is not evidence of what is currently required
dominance_rules.trigger: a renewal, notice, cancellation or payment practice rests on how it has always been done
dominance_rules.action: name the obligation class, verify its current content with the applicable regulator and counsel, and design to the stricter of that and the operator's policy

dominance_rules.rule: The account record dominates the stated reason when the two disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: customers give the reason that ends the call politely, while the visit, callback and communication history shows what actually happened
dominance_rules.trigger: a stated cancellation reason conflicts with the account's own history
dominance_rules.action: record both, drive remediation from the record, and keep the customer's words for what they reveal about the experience

dominance_rules.rule: Density-weighted value dominates raw account count in every keep, reprice and release decision
dominance_rules.rationale: a buyer, a partner operator and the route itself inherit drive time along with revenue, so scattered accounts are worth less than their count suggests
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision is being argued on the number of accounts gained or lost
dominance_rules.action: re-argue it on stops per pass, zone density, survival and callback load before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: A sourced mechanism dominates any figure
dominance_rules.rationale: commissions, prices, retention rates, attachment rates and book multiples vary by market, operator, season and negotiation, and quoting one as fact misleads every decision built on it
dominance_rules.trigger: a commission, price, retention percentage or account multiple is about to be stated or relied on
dominance_rules.action: state the mechanism and its drivers, attach the source in the operator's or the seller's own records, and get any multiple from the actual counterparty in the actual deal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the agreement's promise inventory before writing any sales, retention or save script
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scripts that promise past the paper and produce disputes that then have to be settled account by account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Disclose the initial charge, term, renewal behavior and cancellation route before signature, not in the follow-up
anti_rework_rules.prevents: first-invoice disputes, chargebacks and early cancellations that consume the account before it repays anything

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture access facts at the sale rather than after the first failed visit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: partial visits, disputed charges and reschedules that dilute a route day and get logged as price cancellations

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the frequency class from documented pressure and the route calendar before quoting anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an interval that has to be renegotiated once the route cannot serve it or the pressure rebuilds between visits

anti_rework_rules.rule: Warn about the post-treatment activity surge before the initial service is performed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a first-window callback becoming a cancellation and, in a referral model, a reversed commission

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stand up the per-visit evidence loop before any add-on is offered
anti_rework_rules.prevents: upsell conversations with nothing to point at, which either fail or drift toward invented findings

anti_rework_rules.rule: Instrument cancellation reasons before designing any save remedies
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building remedies and concessions for the wrong defect while the real one keeps producing departures

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the servicing operator can deliver a remedy or an add-on class before it enters the ladder or the catalogue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a promised save or sold program failing a second time, which loses the account and the neighbors it talks to

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the system of record with the partner operator before the first account is signed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unprovable book at separation, when the party without records has nothing transferable whatever the agreement says

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cluster separate-trip add-ons geographically before selling them, and read the churn response on one segment before repricing the whole book
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dedicated passes for single households and a book-wide price move whose cancellations arrive all at once with nothing left to learn from

iteration_protocol.trigger: cohort survival worsens in the first recurring visits
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the surge warning, the initial-service expectation setting and the proactive follow-up contact, and re-check callback priority for accounts inside the window

iteration_protocol.trigger: cancellation reasons cluster on service execution for a route day, a zone or a technician
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile stated reasons against visit and callback records, fix the access or scheduling defect at its source, and escalate a repeat-callback premise to the operator for structural inspection

iteration_protocol.trigger: payment-failure retirements rise as a share of departures
iteration_protocol.action: tighten failure detection and the contact window, re-confirm stored authorizations affected by amount or term changes, and keep the involuntary category separated in every retention view

iteration_protocol.trigger: a regulator, counsel or the operator changes renewal, notice, cancellation-route or stored-authorization requirements
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the obligation classes, update the disclosure set, the renewal notice and the cancellation route, and re-check the nominated-contact practice for accounts under care rules

iteration_protocol.trigger: a season closes and its add-on results are in
iteration_protocol.action: review each class against its pressure window and its qualification evidence, relabel ride-along versus separate-trip work from what actually happened on the route, and retire a class the operator cannot reliably deliver

iteration_protocol.trigger: a price wave's measured churn exceeds what the pilot segment predicted
iteration_protocol.action: halt the next segment, re-read the reasons behind the departures, restore defect remedies ahead of concessions, and re-time the remaining waves to later renewal dates

iteration_protocol.trigger: a zone's density falls below what its route day needs, whether through pauses, releases or moves
iteration_protocol.action: re-run triage for the zone, count paused accounts separately, decide reschedule, reprice, step-down or release for each remaining account, and feed the result back into which frequency classes are sold there

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint alleges that a customer did not understand a renewal, a charge or a save conversation
iteration_protocol.action: pull the disclosure, consent and communication records for the account, stop billing activity while it is reviewed, process any cancellation without a save attempt, and audit the scripts and records that allowed it

priority_rationale: The agreement nodes come first because every retention, save, upsell and valuation claim downstream is an assertion about a term the paper fixes and a disclosure the customer received; the economics and the guarantee follow because they explain why the first visits are the dangerous ones and what the recurring promise actually costs; the retention machine of visible evidence, contact rhythm and frictionless access sits next because it is what keeps accounts alive long enough to matter; measurement and the reason taxonomy precede the save practice so remedies are aimed at diagnosed defects rather than at price; seasonal add-ons come after the evidence loop because a qualified offer depends on findings already recorded; and record hygiene, book valuation and triage come last because they compose everything above into an asset that can be measured, defended, transferred and kept dense while it grows.
